correctness.rationale: Fix r and choose t outside the proper elementary subfield P. If t were algebraic over P, its minimal polynomial over P would have a root in P by elementarity, forcing it to be linear. Therefore 1,t,…,t^(r−1) are P-linearly independent. The map P^r→R that sends (p_i) to Σ_i p_i t^i is definable with parameters and injective. Requiring its unique i-th coefficient to equal a specified element of an infinite sequence in P gives the stated definable cosets, with row-disjointness and explicit simultaneous realization of every selection. In fact, row-disjointness also witnesses the negations required by a depth-r ICT pattern. Thus the finite unary lower bounds hold, without assuming any infinite-depth pattern or an infinite-rank complete type. RCF is o-minimal and geometric (in particular it eliminates ∃∞), and has unary dp-rank 1. For any k≥1 take r=k+1 in the pair, which is NIP by the established preservation result. RCF is then in C_k and its pair is not. Theorem 10.33 of Kim would preserve membership if C_k belonged to the larger indicated class, yielding the contradiction. The frozen verification was inspected; the audit is analytic.

value.rationale: This is a motivated obstruction to preservation of an entire family of finite cutoffs, not a rank calculation for an arbitrary small example. It shows how adding a predicate can encode arbitrarily many independent coordinates into one variable while staying NIP, and supplies a uniform witness against placing bounded unary dp-rank among Kim's pair-preserved dividing lines. The result answers this boundary question even though the field-pair witness and the final preservation application are short.
